idiom_name: move semantics by default; do not implement Copy (or Clone)
implementation_notes: Rust already is the pattern: a type is move-only unless it opts into `Copy`, so `let b = a;` moves and using `a` afterwards is error E0382 ('borrow of moved value'), and the mixin's job is done by not deriving or implementing `Copy` - plus not implementing `Clone` when duplication must be impossible. `Copy` cannot be implemented at all for a type that implements `Drop` or contains a non-`Copy` field, which is exactly the resource-owning case, so RAII types (File, TcpStream, MutexGuard, Box) are non-copyable by construction and duplicate only if the author writes `Clone`. There is no inheritance to hang a mixin on; `PhantomPinned` (`!Unpin`) is the next rung when the value must not even be moved in memory, with `Pin` expressing that as a type invariant.
pitfalls: `Clone` and `Copy` are independent: `Copy` implies `Clone`, but a type can be `Clone` without `Copy`, so blocking only `Copy` still leaves the explicit duplication path - leave `Clone` unimplemented, or implement it as a documented `try_clone()` for OS handles.
Deriving `Copy` is impossible for a type with a `Drop` impl, but deriving `Clone` on a resource type compiles happily and duplicates the handle; the derive line is the review point.
Moving out of a shared reference is impossible, so non-copyable types push work into ownership transfer (`&mut`, `Option::take`, `mem::replace`) and force API changes rather than local patches.
A panic between taking a value out and putting a replacement back can leave an `Option` in its `None` state; prefer `mem::take`/`Option::take` over manual two-step moves.
